brief.analystNote: BTC at $75,857 is holding Phase B territory by a 3.7% margin above the critical 200d SMA / Phase A→B threshold at $73,176, but the weight of evidence is bearish: ETF flows delivered a -$412M print on Nov 6 (2.56x below the $264M/day baseline), LTH net selling averages -5,021 BTC/day over 7 days (regime DISTRIBUTING), the 30-day auction profile is in confirmed IMBALANCE_DOWN with 3/3 closes below the VAL at $78,433, and the macro environment combines a 4.86% 10Y yield, VIX 25.6, and a strengthening dollar — the worst three-factor macro configuration for BTC in this cycle. The one structural positive is MVRV at 1.406 (fair value, not distressed) and zero funding rates (no forced liquidation risk), which suggest this is mid-cycle consolidation rather than bear-market breakdown — but consolidation can extend significantly before resolution. Market regime note: phase anchors are derived with only 13 cycles of history (NORMAL derivation, insufficient for bear-realized and bear-sma rules requiring 120 and 240 cycles respectively), meaning the phase system carries wider confidence intervals than a mature dataset would provide — the $73,176 floor should be treated as directionally reliable but not statistically hardened. The discipline today is patience: preserve the DCA reserve for either a confirmed reclaim of $78,433 (VAL) on two daily closes with positive ETF flows, or a Phase A re-entry below $73,176 — do not add size in the current IMBALANCE_DOWN environment between those two levels.
brief.riskWarning: A daily close below $73,176 (200d SMA / Phase A→B line) on continued ETF outflows would confirm Phase A re-entry, invalidating the BREAKOUT thesis and requiring full portfolio protocol re-evaluation including hard stop monitoring at $52,326.
